overview: Israel is a country in Western Asia, on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea. It declared independence in 1948. Israel considers Jerusalem its capital, but the city's status is disputed and most countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv. Hebrew is the official language, and Arabic has a special status. The land is sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians remains unresolved.

geography.text: Israel is small but varied. A fertile coastal plain runs along the Mediterranean, hills rise inland, and the Jordan Rift Valley runs down the east, containing the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, the lowest place on land on Earth. The south is the Negev desert, which reaches the Red Sea at Eilat.

history.text: The land has a long history for Jewish, Christian and Muslim peoples. After the Ottoman Empire, Britain ruled Palestine from 1920. In 1948 Israel declared independence; in the war that followed, around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were driven from their homes. Israel has fought several wars with its neighbours, made peace with Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994, and its conflict with the Palestinians continues.

events.title: Balfour Declaration
events.text: Britain supports a 'national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Israel declares independence; war with its Arab neighbours follows.

events.title: Six-Day War
events.text: Israel takes the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and the Golan Heights.

events.title: Peace with Egypt
events.text: Israel and Egypt sign a peace treaty.

events.title: Peace with Jordan
events.text: Israel and Jordan sign a peace treaty.

events.title: War in Gaza
events.text: A Hamas attack on Israel is followed by a devastating war in Gaza.
